places.name: Le Comptoir du Relais
places.verdict: The birthplace of bistronomy. No reservations needed, food served all day, and a Saint-Germain location that makes it dangerously convenient.

comparison.strengths: 4.1★ from 1,403 reviews · No reservations needed · Food served all day · Created by Yves Camdeborde (father of bistronomy)
comparison.limitations: Can get crowded at peak hours · Saint-Germain prices
comparison.why it made the list: Yves Camdeborde opened Le Comptoir in 2004 and essentially invented the bistronomy movement — haute cuisine techniques at bistro prices. The daytime walk-in format makes it one of the most accessible great bistros in Paris.
comparison.what to order: Roast lamb or daube Provençale. The menu changes seasonally — trust whatever's on the chalkboard.

places.whatToOrder: Roast lamb or daube Provençale. The menu changes seasonally — trust whatever's on the chalkboard.

places.editorialSummary: The birthplace of bistronomy. No reservations needed, food served all day, and a Saint-Germain location that makes it dangerously convenient.

places.verdict: The best deal in Paris dining. Three courses of honest French food for €15 in a gorgeous Montmartre setting. The 52,000+ reviews speak for themselves.

comparison.strengths: 4.6★ from 52,718 reviews · Three courses for €15 · Beautiful interior · Traditional 19th century bouillon format

comparison.why it made the list: 52,718 Google reviews with a 4.6 rating is almost unheard of for a restaurant. places.name: Bouillon Chartier
places.verdict: A Belle Époque time capsule serving budget French food since 1896. Come for the jaw-dropping dining hall; the food is honest and cheap.

comparison.best for: Historic dining experience on a budget — the most beautiful cheap meal in Paris
comparison.strengths: 4.1★ from 31,282 reviews · Operating since 1896 · Stunning Belle Époque interior · Budget prices
comparison.limitations: Food is good, not exceptional — you're paying for the experience · No reservations · Can feel rushed
comparison.why it made the list: Operating continuously since 1896, Chartier is a living piece of Paris history. The grand Belle Époque dining hall — mirrored walls, brass fixtures, white-aproned waiters — is worth visiting for the atmosphere alone. The food is classic and cheap: onion soup, steak-frites, crème caramel.
comparison.what to order: Soupe à l'oignon gratinée to start, steak-frites or roast chicken for the main, crème caramel to finish. The whole meal runs €12-18.
